# Churchill Downs Stakes Advances: Unbeaten Travers Stakes Winner Leading Change Returns in Friday's $700,000 Clark; Dual Grade I Winner Tam Tam Headlines $300,000 Mrs. Revere


## Nov 20, 2026


Wathnan Racing’s unbeaten Travers winner Leading Change will take on older horses in the 152nd running of the $700,000 Clark presented by Norton Healthcare (Grade II), the featured race of the 2026 Fall Meet at Churchill Downs.


Contested at 1 1/8 miles for 3-year-olds and up, the Clark shares Friday’s spotlight with the 35th running of the $300,000 Mrs. Revere (GII). First post for the 12-race program is 1 p.m. (all times Eastern), with the 1 1/8-mile Clark scheduled as Race 11 at 5:54 p.m. and the Mrs. Revere as Race 10 at 5:25 p.m.


Trained by Brad Cox, Leading Change won his June 7 debut at Churchill Downs by 6 ½ lengths and followed with a neck victory in the $300,000 Indiana Derby (GIII) at Horseshoe Indianapolis. The 3-year-old son of Gun Runner improved to 3-for-3 in the $1.25 million Travers (GI) on Aug. 29 at Saratoga when he defeated Preakness winner Napoleon Solo by a half-length. Leading Change will be ridden in the Clark by Manny Franco out of post No. 2


Cox also entered Juddmonte’s Dragoon Guard, a 5-year-old son of Arrogate who scored a 3 ¼-length victory in the $500,000 Lukas Classic (GII) on Sept. 26 at Churchill Downs. Tyler Gaffalione rides from post 5.


Paradise Farms Corp. and Case Chambers’ Willy D’s enters the race off a neck victory over Stars and Stripes in the $350,000 Fayette (GIII) on Oct. 24 at Keeneland. The 5-year-old gelding, trained by Mike Maker, also won the $1 million Charles Town Classic (GII) and the $300,000 TwinSpires Kentucky Cup Classic (GIII) this year. Hall of Famer John Velazquez has the call from post 8.


With a victory, Velazquez would tie Isaac Murphy and Pat Day for the most wins in the Clark by a jockey with four. Velazquez previously won the Clark aboard Magna Graduate (2005), Wise Dan (2011) and Seeking the Soul (2017).


Also entered in the Clark are $1 million Breeders’ Cup Dirt Mile (GI) competitors Bracket Buster and Chunk of Gold.


BBN Racing and Bowen Thoroughbred Racing’s Bracket Buster finished seventh in the Dirt Mile. The 4-year-old son of Vekoma won the $200,000 West Virginia Governor’s Stakes (Listed) by 15 lengths in his first start of the year for trainer Vicki Oliver and finished second in the $300,000 Parx Dirt Mile (Listed) in September. He was second to eventual Horse of the Year Sovereignty in last year’s Travers. Junior Alvarado will be in the irons and exit post 9.


BBN Racing and Oliver previously teamed up to win the race in 2023 with Trademark, who pulled a 13-1 upset over 6-5 favorite First Mission.


Terry Stephens’ Chunk of Gold, third in last year’s Clark behind Magnitude and Hit Show, finished second to Dragoon Guard in the Lukas Classic before running ninth in the Dirt Mile. Trained by Ethan West, the 4-year-old millionaire son of Preservationist will reunite with Jaime Torres and break from post 10.

DUAL GRADE I WINNER TAM TAM HEADLINES $300,000 MRS. REVERE – Rigney Racing’s Tam Tam, whose three-race winning streak includes back-to-back Grade I victories in the $300,000 Del Mar Oaks and $750,000 Queen Elizabeth II Challenge Cup, returns to Churchill Downs next Friday to headline the 35th running of the $300,000 Mrs. Revere (Grade II).


The 1 1/16-mile turf race for 3-year-old fillies shares Friday’s spotlight with the $700,000 Clark presented by Norton Healthcare (GII). First post is 1 p.m., with the Mrs. Revere scheduled as Race 10 of 12 at 5:25 p.m. and the Clark as Race 11 at 5:54 p.m.


Trained by Phil Bauer, Tam Tam began her streak with a 5 ¾-length victory in the $275,000 Tepin (Listed) on June 27 at Churchill Downs. The daughter of Medaglia d’Oro followed with a 1 ¼-length win in the Aug. 22 Del Mar Oaks before leading throughout the Oct. 10 Queen Elizabeth II Challenge Cup at Keeneland, where she beat Faithful Departed by 2 ½ lengths. Overall, Tam Tam has won five of seven starts since switching to turf in February and earned more than $1 million in 10 career starts. Junior Alvarado, who’s been aboard Tam Tam for her last six starts, returns to the saddle Friday from post No. 5.


Also entered in the Mrs. Revere is Woodslane Racing’s six-time winner Sister Troienne. Trained by Brian Lynch, Sister Troienne recently scored a two-length victory in the $400,000 Valley View (GII) at Keeneland under Luis Saez. Earlier in the season, the daughter of Munnings scored a trio of stakes victories at Gulfstream Park before finishing second in the $200,000 Herecomesthebride (GIII) and $200,000 Winter Memories (GIII). Sister Troienne will break from post 6 with Saez aboard.
